Cardiac arrest and OHCA.recommendation: A PPCI strategy is recommended in patients with resuscitated cardiac arrest and an ECG with persistent ST-segment elevation (or equivalents).
Cardiac arrest and OHCA.notes: References indicated on page for supporting evidence.

Cardiac arrest and OHCA.recommendation: Routine immediate angiography after resuscitated cardiac arrest is not recommended in haemodynamically stable patients without persistent ST-segment elevation (or equivalents).
Cardiac arrest and OHCA.notes: Applies to haemodynamically stable patients without persistent ST-elevation.

Temperature control.recommendation: Temperature control (continuous monitoring of core temperature and active prevention of fever [i.e. >37.7°C]) is recommended after either out-of-hospital or in-hospital cardiac arrest for adults who remain unresponsive after return of spontaneous circulation.

Systems of care.recommendation: Healthcare systems should implement strategies to facilitate transfer of all patients in whom ACS is suspected after resuscitated cardiac arrest directly to a hospital offering 24/7 PPCI via one specialized EMS.
Systems of care.notes: Focus on system-level transfer strategies to PPCI-capable centres.

Systems of care.recommendation: Transport of patients with OHCA to a cardiac arrest centre according to local protocols should be considered.
Systems of care.notes: Consideration for routing OHCA patients to designated cardiac arrest centres.

Evaluation of neurological prognosis.recommendation: Evaluation of neurological prognosis (no earlier than 72 h after admission) is recommended in all comatose survivors after cardiac arrest.
Evaluation of neurological prognosis.notes: Timing: not earlier than 72 hours after admission.
